subject.title: feat(tui): inline image rendering via pi-tui Image component

question: Should TUI inline rendering read absolute MEDIA paths in the host process, or should it only render trusted structured image blocks and media-store references from current OpenClaw media contracts?
rationale: The feature is useful, but the submitted shape crosses from model/tool text into local host file reads and terminal graphics output, which is a product and security boundary choice automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Render trusted structured media only
options.body: Require the implementation to consume current image blocks or structured generated-attachment/media-store references and avoid arbitrary absolute host path reads.

options.title: Allow constrained absolute MEDIA reads
options.body: Permit the PR’s path-read approach only with explicit trusted-root policy, tests, documentation, and live proof across local and Docker gateway setups.

options.title: Pause under the canonical tracker
options.body: Keep the feature tracked in the canonical issue while closing or parking this draft until a maintainer sponsors the security boundary.

recommendation.title: Render trusted structured media only
recommendation.body: Require the implementation to consume current image blocks or structured generated-attachment/media-store references and avoid arbitrary absolute host path reads.

likelyOwner.reason: The current TUI renderer history and adjacent image_generate introduction make steipete the best available routing owner for this boundary decision.
